_runtimeCompression: 1, AND IT IS A DECISION. Compressing this block means scaling ten DB_Settings presets that are Real seconds read at run time (FB_ShredderSequencer NETWORK 2 converts every one), plus the motor block's ReverseDelay = 8.0 s and FTTime = 10.0 s, plus this head's three 15 s cleardown dwells - and the head's dwells were derived as the smallest round number above the longest settling constant in the loop, so scaling one without the other breaks the cleardown. blockCompression is therefore OMITTED, which at comp = 1 is contract section 2.4's 'CHECKED, a real pass' row: nothing is scaled, so none of X-D's three ceilings can bind. It is not an omission and it is not NOT CHECKED. The cost is wall-clock: each index here is 150-165 s.
_waveGeometry: OVER-DECLARED ON PURPOSE, AND THE PERMISSIVE DIRECTION IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE INTUITIVE ONE. Section 12a derivation 1's correction of 2026-08-14 states it plainly: over-declaring slots gives a floor that is too HIGH and is conservative; UNDER-declaring is what admits an unobservable window, and a submission declaring 1 while running in a wider wave gets a floor roughly a third of the true one, with the symptom being a missed assertion reported as a pass. This slot cannot run alone - harness-binding.json's unresolvedHoles requires it to be merged with the hopper and pusher documents into one multi-slot binding first - so 3 is the smallest honest wave, and 24 is this slot's own result-source count. At W=24 the read plan is floor(125/24) = 5 whole slots per FC03 read and ceil(3/5) = 1 read cycle, so the multiplier on the floor is 1 and the sampled floor stays 9 scans. Every windowScans here clears it by two orders of magnitude, so the figure is not load-bearing for any expectation in this set - which is stated so nobody reads the margin as care.

vectors._scenario: PRESTART_THEN_DISCHARGE. The head holds the plant idle-but-healthy for 5 s, presses cycle-start for 1 s, and the sequencer leaves the idle step. The pre-start siren then runs its full 10 s (DB_Settings.PreStartSounderTime = 10.0) before the discharge conveyor is commanded at t = 15 s. The modelled discharge contactor confirms 2 s later, inside the 10 s DischargeConveyorTimeout, so the sequence advances and the discharge command stays asserted for the rest of the scenario. The hopper is commanded HIGH for the whole scenario (HopperHighAt 0, HopperClearAt at the scenario end), which holds the infeed restart timer off and keeps the infeed and upstream-enable outputs out of this vector entirely - isolation, not convenience. No stop lever is set and StopAt is at the scenario end, so no commanded stop fires.
vectors._timeline: ms from the start of the scenario, which is the instant the 45 s head cleardown finishes: 0 idle - 5000 cycle-start pressed - 5000..15000 DQ10_SYS_PreStartSounder asserted (10 s) - 15000 DQ5_DIS_Run asserted - 17000 discharge running confirmed - 17000..32000 reverse step (the motor block's own ReverseDelay = 8.0 s entry pause, then 1 s to confirmed reverse, then 6 s of confirmed reverse run) - ~34000 running step - 60000 scenario ends. DQ5 is asserted from 15000 to 60000, DQ10 from 5000 to 15000.

blacklist.reason: MEASURED COLLISION, NOT A PRECAUTION. This slot's head needs DB_Input.Test[0,1,3,4,5,6,7,8,10,15] and writes every one with the pass-through idiom; FB_HopperBlockageStim writes Test[0,5,6,8] with NO pass-through on any (recorded in harness-binding.json _slotContention, scanned per-index out of the IR because converter reachable-state reports DB_Input.Test at whole-array granularity). Idle it drives all four low, and the heads run in sequence ahead of the input map, so whichever runs last in the sweep wins. Test[5] and Test[6] are the shredder running feedbacks this slot's whole timeline is built on.

It passes through on all 8 of its own indices, so the Test[] array is safe - but this head's NETWORK 26 writes DB_Controls.PusherMode with a PLAIN MOVE and no pass-through, and the pusher head and block both read that member. Two lanes driving one operator-mode member is last-writer-wins, and the pusher-quiet assumption behind this slot's PreStartSounder reading is exactly what it breaks.

It consumes Hopper_Level_High and the shredder running feedbacks, all three of which this head commands, so running it concurrently means this slot's stimulus is driving that block's plant model. Coupling through plant-model state that the reference graph does not see, which is contract section 7's own case.

It consumes hopper-high as an auto-mode cycle trigger and it consumes this block's PusherParkCmd, PusherCycleInhibitCmd and PusherModeCmd. Same plant-model coupling, and it is additionally the source of IO.PusherJogPreStartSounder, the second term of the signal SHR-001 asserts on.

vectors._scenario: HOPPER_CLEARS_THEN_INFEED_THEN_UPSTREAM. The same start, but the hopper is commanded high from the start of the scenario until t = 45 s, which is comfortably after the sequence has reached its running step at about t = 34 s. The hopper then reads clear, the 5 s InfeedRestartDelay runs, the infeed conveyor is commanded at t = 50 s, and the 3 s InfeedToUpstreamEnableDelay runs on top of it so upstream is enabled at t = 53 s. Both outputs are then asserted for the remaining 22 s of the scenario. No stop lever is set.
vectors._timeline: ms from the start of the scenario: 0 idle, hopper HIGH - 5000 cycle-start pressed - 15000 discharge commanded - ~34000 running step reached, infeed restart timer held off by the high hopper - 45000 hopper reads clear, restart timer starts - 50000 DQ4_IFC_Run asserted - 53000 DQ9_SYS_EnableUpstream asserted - 75000 scenario ends. DQ4 is asserted from 50000 to 75000, DQ9 from 53000 to 75000.

blacklist.reason: MEASURED COLLISION, NOT A PRECAUTION. This slot's head needs DB_Input.Test[0,1,3,4,5,6,7,8,10,15] and writes every one with the pass-through idiom; FB_HopperBlockageStim writes Test[0,5,6,8] with NO pass-through on any (recorded in harness-binding.json _slotContention, scanned per-index out of the IR because converter reachable-state reports DB_Input.Test at whole-array granularity). Idle it drives all four low, and the heads run in sequence ahead of the input map, so whichever runs last in the sweep wins. Test[5] and Test[6] are the shredder running feedbacks this slot's whole timeline is built on.

It passes through on all 8 of its own indices, so the Test[] array is safe - but this head's NETWORK 26 writes DB_Controls.PusherMode with a PLAIN MOVE and no pass-through, and the pusher head and block both read that member. Two lanes driving one operator-mode member is last-writer-wins, and the pusher-quiet assumption behind this slot's PreStartSounder reading is exactly what it breaks.

It consumes Hopper_Level_High and the shredder running feedbacks, all three of which this head commands, so running it concurrently means this slot's stimulus is driving that block's plant model. Coupling through plant-model state that the reference graph does not see, which is contract section 7's own case.

It consumes hopper-high as an auto-mode cycle trigger and it consumes this block's PusherParkCmd, PusherCycleInhibitCmd and PusherModeCmd. Same plant-model coupling, and it is additionally the source of IO.PusherJogPreStartSounder, the second term of the signal SHR-001 asserts on.

vectors.kills: AN IMPLEMENTATION THAT NEVER ENABLES UPSTREAM - the plant recovers from a full hopper, the infeed restarts, and the upstream process is never told it may feed, so the plant runs empty. That mutant reads DQ9_SYS_EnableUpstream false in every retained frame and returns Disagreed while DQ4 still passes. It also kills a mutant whose hopper gate is latched rather than level-driven, so clearing the hopper never restarts the infeed: DQ4 then reads false throughout, and BOTH expectations go red, which distinguishes it from the first mutant. *** WHAT IT DOES NOT KILL: *** a block that enables upstream in the SAME instant as the infeed, with no delay at all. That is REQ-011:71f815 - the enumeration's own note says A1 is satisfied by an early enable that is still asserted at t = 3 s, which is why the two assertions exist separately - and it is a Never, which this slot cannot verify. The most valuable half of REQ-011 is therefore NOT covered here, and this vector must not be read as covering the clause. Not run against either mutant; argued from the IR.

_observabilityShortfall: *** THE PRINCIPAL FINDING OF THIS RUN, AND IT IS ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN OPINION. 41 OF THE 43 ASSERTIONS CANNOT BE CITED BY ANY VECTOR AGAINST THIS SLOT AS IT IS BOUND, AND NOT ONE OF THE FOUR CAUSES IS REPAIRABLE BY A VECTOR AUTHOR. *** CAUSE 1 - THE PHYSICAL OUTPUTS THE SPECIFICATION IS WRITTEN IN ARE MOSTLY NOT PUBLISHED. Of the six DQ names the enumeration cites, this binding publishes four (DQ5_DIS_Run, DQ4_IFC_Run, DQ9_SYS_EnableUpstream, DQ10_SYS_PreStartSounder) and CANNOT publish two: FC_ControlMain NETWORK 7 takes DQ1_SHR_RunFwd and DQ2_SHR_RunRev from iDB_MotorFwdRevSystem_Shredder.IO.RunFwd and .RunRev, which are not in resultSources. DQ1 appears in 22 of the 43 assertions' required observations and DQ2 in 22. CAUSE 2 - NO INPUT IS PUBLISHED AT ALL. The enumeration's assertions require observing DI8_HPR_LevelHigh (11 times), DI3_SYS_CycleStart (8), DI15_SYS_DownstreamRunning (5), DI10_DIS_Running (3), DI4_SYS_CycleStop (2), and DI1/DI5/DI6/DI9/DI12 once each. The binding publishes none of them, although eight of the ten exist as members of iDB_ShredderSequencer.IO and are INSIDE the binding's own declared --scope prefix. Gate 3h is a set difference and it is not negotiable: AMB-14's whole point is that a relational assertion whose second signal is never observed is untested while everything reports green. CAUSE 3 - EVERY `Never` IS INADMISSIBLE, ALL 16 OF THEM. F-3 refuses a SAMPLED observation of a NEVER assertion - the refusal is live in Harness.Loop.LoopRun's own caveat text - so a Never needs Latched, Latched needs a generated latch (Transient + ArmedBy) or a genuine instrumenting block, and this binding declares neither. Its three latchedBy entries name the block under test and a block inside the stimulated loop, which section 2.8 rules is a value under test rather than an instrument. CAUSE 4 - NO ARM WINDOW, SO ONLY ONE TEMPORAL SHAPE CAN CONCLUDE. With no armedBy, every retained frame is WindowState.Unknown, and the accusation rule in docs/notes/observation-window-shapes.md section 2 turns throughout, becomesAndHolds and atNoPoint into Inconclusive on any mixed series - and the head's mandatory tail cleardown makes EVERY commanded state a mixed series by construction. That is why both vectors here use atSomePoint, and why neither can say anything about ORDER. *** WHAT WOULD FIX MOST OF IT, AND IT IS ONE ARTIFACT: *** ten more result sources on the binding - iDB_MotorFwdRevSystem_Shredder.IO.RunFwd and .RunRev, and iDB_ShredderSequencer.IO.CycleStart, .CycleStop, .DownstreamRunning, .SystemHealthy, .HopperLevelHigh, .DischargeConvRunning, .ShredderRunFwdFB and .ShredderRunRevFB - each with an inertRest, plus Transient and ArmedBy (SHR.Armed is already published) on the signals a Never has to be read from. Every one of those is derivable from the corpus. NONE of them is this lane's field: inertRest is section 2.8b's and the observability declaration is declaredBy's, and this lane was instructed not to touch either. DI9_IFC_Running would still be missing - the sequencer does not consume it - so REQ-063's infeed instance stays unreachable through this slot however the binding grows.
_unreachable: *** THE UNREACHABLE-CANDIDATE BUCKET LIST, BY ASSERTION ID. THESE ARE CITED AS UNREACHABLE, NOT AS SATISFIED, AND THE BUCKETING IS THE ENGINEER'S CALL, NOT THIS LANE'S. *** ELEVEN assertions trigger on an overcurrent event that no stimulus can produce: REQ-023:d9f51c, REQ-024:f6a85d, REQ-025:5c6fe9, REQ-026:dc4fd2, REQ-027:229d37, REQ-027:f8f777, REQ-027:99d80f, REQ-028:bda7cd, REQ-028:567ac6, REQ-028:3e10c1, REQ-028:3f419e. THE MEASURED REASON: FB_ShredderSequencer NETWORK 12 gates both OvercurrentMediumTimer and OvercurrentHighTimer on 'AND NOT AlwaysTrue', a permanently false placeholder the block's own OvercurrentTripped comment declares - so OvercurrentTripped can never be true, the only transition into step 60 (N12's third MOVE) can never fire, and with it die all three of N13's transitions, N3's window timer, N4's reversal counter, N5's ShredderBlockedFault seal and the step-60 term of PusherModeForceOff in N14. IT IS DEAD TWICE OVER: even with the placeholder removed, DB_Settings.OvercurrentSetpointMedium/High and the two delays are deliberately unconfigured (Q-11: this prototype panel carries no analog current channel), and IO.ShredderMotorCurrent is a Real while MirrorValueType carries Bool, Int and Time only, so the analog input cannot be commanded through the mirror even after the detection is armed. *** NOT ONE VECTOR IN THIS SET ASSERTS THAT iDB_ShredderSequencer.IO.ShredderBlockedFault IS CLEAR, AND THAT IS THE POINT. *** N5 makes it a compile-time-constant false, so ANY assertion of the form 'the shredder-blocked fault is clear' would pass forever, vacuously, and it would pass more convincingly than the pusher's equivalent because the surrounding sequence really does run. A green over it would be the single most misleading output this slot can produce. The signal is published in the binding and carries a specName so a reader can see it, and its _specName says in terms that no vector may cite it. REQ-028:567ac6 CARRIES A SECOND, INDEPENDENT BLOCK: its response_signal is the literal UNNAMED_IN_REGISTER. FINDING-2 records that the register names no tag for any annunciation bit. It is uncitable even if the overcurrent path were armed, and hard rule 3 forbids inventing a name to make the citation join. The repair is to the REGISTER, never to the enumeration and never to a vector.

(a) REQ-012:4c5d5a and REQ-013:5eebb6 are SIMULTANEITY claims - 'at the same time' - and contract section 4.1 says a same-scan coincidence is unobservable by sampling at all. (b) The other 28 are blocked by _observabilityShortfall's four causes, which are BINDING repairs: they are not untestable, they are unobservable as currently bound, and calling them UNTESTABLE-ON-RIG would freeze a fixable gap into a bucket. _decompositionDisputes: RAISED AS THE FIRST PARTY TO HAVE READ THIS ENUMERATION AGAINST THE IMPLEMENTATION. THREE, AND ONLY THE FIRST IS A DISAGREEMENT. DISPUTE 1 - REQ-063's BOUND IS ONE NAME DOING FOUR JOBS, AND THE ONE INSTANCE THAT IS TESTABLE IS THE ONE THE NAME IS WRONG FOR. assertionBounds gives REQ-063:f94e84 the single bound motor_run_confirm_time, whose table row is the sentence 'UNSPECIFIED for three of REQ-063's four declared instances'. But the clause declares FOUR instances and the DischargeConveyor one has a real, distinct, named bound - discharge_conveyor_timeout = 10 s, already in the same table - implemented and live in FB_ShredderSequencer NETWORK 8. As it stands a vector for that instance must declare boundsUsed against a row that says UNSPECIFIED, which is true of three instances and false of the one being tested; declaring the real bound instead is refused as a bound the assertion does not depend on. THE PROPOSED REPAIR IS TO assertionBounds, NOT TO ANY ASSERTION TEXT AND NOT TO ANY ID: make the bound instance-qualified, so the DischargeConveyor unit depends on discharge_conveyor_timeout and the other three on the UNSPECIFIED row. That moves zero hashes. FINDING-3 already says the substance; this is the mechanical consequence it does not draw, and it bites the moment cause 1 and cause 2 above are repaired and REQ-063 becomes citable. DISPUTE 2 - NOT A DISPUTE, A CONFIRMATION FROM THE IMPLEMENTATION SIDE. AMB-SEQ-04 says a plant that stops everything while still telling upstream to feed passes every assertion in the file. It does, and the block makes it concrete rather than hypothetical: FB_ShredderSequencer NETWORK 11 drives IO.EnableUpstream purely from UpstreamEnableTimer.Q, whose IN is InfeedRunning, whose own timer IN is 'IO.Step = 50 AND NOT IO.HopperLevelHigh'. A stop drives Step to 0, so the enable does in fact drop - but by side effect of the step condition, with no stop term anywhere in its own rung. The hole AMB-SEQ-04 names is real AND the as-built block happens to be right for a reason no assertion states. That is the worst combination for a later edit. DISPUTE 3 - NOT A DISPUTE. AMB-SEQ-07 asks what the fifth overcurrent event does, and AMB-SEQ-08 asks whether a start-sequence reverse counts. NEITHER CAN BE SETTLED FROM THIS IMPLEMENTATION IN EITHER DIRECTION, because N4 counts entries into step 60 and step 60 is unreachable - so the block has no observable answer to give and a reader must not take its silence for one. Recorded because 'the code does X' is the usual way these get closed, and here it would be closing them on a network that never executes.
_whatThisSetDoesNotEstablish: SAID PLAINLY, BECAUSE A TWO-VECTOR GREEN IS EASY TO OVER-READ. Both vectors use temporalShape atSomePoint, which establishes that a signal WAS asserted somewhere in the retained series and says NOTHING about when, in what order, or for how long. So this set does not establish: that the pre-start siren runs before any equipment starts (REQ-003:045ab4, a Never); that the discharge conveyor's FEEDBACK gates the sequence rather than its own command (REQ-004:0f72e0, a Never); that upstream is not enabled early (REQ-011:71f815, a Never, and the enumeration's own note explains that REQ-011 A1 is SATISFIED by the early-enable defect); or anything at all about stopping, re-starting, hopper recovery, the two-tier pusher split, or the fault-abort paths. THE MOST DEFECT-PRONE LOGIC IN THIS BLOCK - the REQ-012/013/040 split where downstream loss must inhibit the cycle without taking hand-jog away - IS COMPLETELY UNCOVERED, because every assertion over it requires observing DQ1_SHR_RunFwd, DQ2_SHR_RunRev or a DI, and because IO.PusherCycleInhibitCmd and IO.PusherModeCmd have no specification name to cite at all.
